title: Source-first mechanical ornithopter interpretation
status: Educational reduced model; not a recovered Stanley design, buildable aircraft, or validated flight prediction.

source_derived_geometry.reading: The rounded 'Say' span is 7.4 ft, wrist span is 3.7 ft (50% of full span), total area is 6.61 ft², and the paragraph prints AR=b²/S=8.29.
source_derived_geometry.exclusion: The nearby 3.135 ft wing-length conversion is internally inconsistent and was not used.
source_derived_geometry.visual_use: Broad constant-chord arm wings lead to rounded, tapered hand wings.

photographs.readable_principle: Swan planform dimensions distinguish shoulder, wrist and full span; area and rounded span establish aspect ratio. The text warns that spread planform and specimens vary.
photographs.unreadable_or_uncertain: Faint handwritten species/reference notes and several marginal corrections are not reliably legible.
photographs.engineering_completion: The model scales the rounded 7.4 ft full span to 14 m, uses AR 8.29 and wrist/full span 3.7/7.4. Four-segment taper and chord normalisation come from the supplied helper.

photographs.readable_principle: A Göttingen 417a curved-plate chart compares lift, drag and moment-like traces at low Reynolds-number labels.
photographs.unreadable_or_uncertain: The rotated multi-axis chart, pencil annotations, exact ordinate mapping and curve provenance cannot support reliable coefficient digitisation.
photographs.engineering_completion: No chart values were transcribed. Inner and outer coefficient tables in engineering.mjs are explicitly favourable illustrative assumptions.

photographs.readable_principle: Define a desired sinusoidal trajectory, infer the required cyclic vertical-force range, and compare candidate wing actions; the stated aim is a powered man-carrying ornithopter.
photographs.unreadable_or_uncertain: The missing appendices and revised equations are unavailable; marginal flight-history note is not treated as design data.
photographs.engineering_completion: The simulation integrates forces rather than prescribing trajectory. The comparison panel remains diagnostic only.

photographs.readable_principle: Straight-level flapping necessarily has cyclic lift and thrust and therefore small undulations; recovery styles can leave intermittent or continuous wake structures.
photographs.unreadable_or_uncertain: Handwritten line above the heading is only partly legible and the reproduced wake is qualitative.
photographs.engineering_completion: Local strip forces vary through the linkage cycle; no wake or free lift is prescribed.

photographs.readable_principle: At low speed the working downstroke lasts longer than recovery; at cruise the periods become equal. Candidate force histories should be compared with required forces, and wing/wishbone/body can be treated as a resonant system.
photographs.unreadable_or_uncertain: Dense marginal revisions around the trajectory paragraph are uncertain and are not promoted to equations.
photographs.engineering_completion: A fixed timing-bias linkage gives low-speed unequal timing and zero-bias cruise timing. Distributed inertia, a hinge spring and finite damping implement energy exchange.

photographs.readable_principle: Wing and body inertia act about the common CG; fore/aft wing motion creates pitching reaction. The hand wing moves up/forward while closed, then down/back while opened, and closes on recovery.
photographs.unreadable_or_uncertain: Crossed-out words and margin comments do not provide numerical linkage dimensions.
photographs.engineering_completion: The helper derives moving CG, inertia and Jacobians from sweep, stroke, twist and overlap. Two rigid outer leaves reduce exposed area while retaining mass.

photographs.readable_principle: The opening continuation says recovery has reduced area/span and local incidences are adjusted. The later goshawk drawing demonstrates that wing regions and section curvature vary.
photographs.unreadable_or_uncertain: The goshawk's printed 13/10/9/6 percent cambers are an example, not swan dimensions, and faint reverse-page text is ignored.
photographs.engineering_completion: Independent incidence/twist and camber curves alter production geometry and section coefficients; supplied amplitudes are assumptions.

photographs.readable_principle: The arm section is about 5–6% thick; the outer hand is a thin slotted curved plate whose high lift/drag is useful on the working stroke and reduced by recovery closing. A conventional tail/rudder or weight shift is compatible.
photographs.unreadable_or_uncertain: Takeoff angle and frequency observations describe birds, not a complete aircraft specification.
photographs.engineering_completion: Inner thickness metadata is 5.5%, outer 0.8%; sliding leaves, tailplane, elevator, fin and rudder are mechanical completions.

photographs.readable_principle: Glide baseline work is drag times speed; powered flight adds induced/aerodynamic, trajectory, acceleration and wing-inertia terms. Zero damping permits inertial exchange rather than net inertial power.
photographs.unreadable_or_uncertain: The handwritten dimensional-analysis notes and absent appendices do not establish a full power budget.
photographs.engineering_completion: Shaft work, aerodynamic dissipation, transmission/damping heat and control work are integrated separately. The spring stores and returns energy but supplies no net propulsion.

engineering_assumptions.mass: 55 kg seated pilot; 173.9 kg dry including pilot; 3.6 kg initial fuel; 177.5 kg initially wet, using the supplied revised budget.
engineering_assumptions.powerplant: The 16 kW continuous shaft limit, governor, starting torque, fuel consumption and 0.85 transmission efficiency are supplied modern assumptions, not Stanley's specifications.
engineering_assumptions.aerodynamics: The coefficient tables, strip discretisation, finite-difference derivatives, tail coefficients and flat-plate drag areas are supplied illustrative completions, not photo digitisation.
engineering_assumptions.mechanism: The exact sinusoidal biased crank curves, spring stiffness, two-leaf overlap, sweep and moving-mass allocations complete ideas that the photographs do not dimension.
engineering_assumptions.glide: Approach speed, pitch and flight-path angle are the supplied numerical equilibrium of the frozen extended model, not notebook readings.

limitations: Quasi-steady strips omit unsteady wakes, section pitching moments, overlap flow interaction, flexible structure and stall hysteresis.
The source's missing appendices and revised calculations remain missing.
Favourable composite masses and ideal linkages have no structural or aeroelastic validation.
The ground model is a reduced rigid three-wheel constraint without suspension.
The visual airframe is an interpretive mechanical translation of swan proportions, not an animal replica.
